Subject: Dedicated capacity request — preemption protection & burst pricing

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We like Redwood’s throughput and the batching controls, but we have two non-standard asks from our infra team that are blockers for the renewal:

1) Preemption protection window for certain queued jobs (we run long inference pipelines and need a straight 4-hour preemption-free window on 10% of our committed pool).
2) A defined burst pricing tier for H100-equivalent capacity that caps overage at a predictable per-hour rate instead of the standard dynamic surcharge.

Attached are our batch profile and a short requirements doc. Can Redwood commit to a firm price cap for burst hours and a contractual protection window? Our procurement timeline is tight — we need a signed term sheet by 2027-02-10 to hit our quarter procurement window.

Appreciate a quick path here.

—Samir

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — preemption protection & burst pricing (feasibility + ask)

Laura / Vivek — read-through and quick take below.

Feasibility (Product):
- 4-hour hard preemption-free window: technically we can reserve a non-preemptible subpool for them, but it requires a dedication on scheduling and impacts overall cluster efficiency. Operationally acceptable if committed pool >= 1.5x their stated baseline for the duration; otherwise we should offer a soft-guarantee (priority queue + monitored credits).
- Burst pricing cap: acceptable as a commercial construct. We should map to a defined burst band (e.g., bursts beyond committed 100% up to 200% charged at capped rate $/GPU-hour). For H100-equivalent, recommend a capped overage of $75/GPU-hour for the first 250 burst hours/month and $95 thereafter — this is conservative and preserves margin.

Recommended language for term sheet (one-liner):
"Redwood will provide a non-preemptible protection window for up to 10% of the Customer's committed capacity for continuous 4-hour periods; bursts beyond committed capacity will be billed at a capped rate of $75/GPU-hour for the first 250 burst hours per month, and $95/GPU-hour thereafter."

Risks/Notes:
- Requires Ops alignment to reserve capacity at scale; potential negative impact on other burst customers during high demand.
- Need Deal Desk approval for guaranteed rates and to accept the margin hit for the first 250 hours.

If we get a thumbs up from Deal Desk (Vivek), I can draft the clause and confirm SLO language for the Console and SLA addendum.

—Rishi
Director, Serving Runtime

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 6 Feb 2027 11:38:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — preemption protection & burst pricing (deal desk decision)

Approved for commercial terms with one amendment.

Decision: Approve the proposed preemption protection and burst pricing cap as drafted, with the following commercial guardrail:
- Cap $75/GPU-hour for first 150 burst hours per month (not 250), then $95/GPU-hour thereafter.
- Include a clause: Customer acknowledges that guaranteed protection windows are subject to scheduled maintenance and must be requested 72 hours in advance for planned maintenance blackout exceptions.
- Offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of the first-month committed invoice if OrionAI signs by 2027-02-09.

Reasoning: Margin sensitivity — we shrink the 150-> to limit downside; onboarding credit helps close. Ops will handle the subpool reservations, but they need the 72-hour maintenance notice.

Next steps: Laura, send the revised one-line term and attach the SLA addendum + DocuSign link. Rishi, please produce the technical SLO wording for Console / tracing and the ops playbook stub. Tessa, loop in Legal if Orion pushes for broader no-preemption language beyond 10%.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Revenue Operations
